dataset_name: Hailey Global Festivals — Year-round Research Catalogue

scope.status: Expanded research draft; not exhaustive; annual dates only materialized where fixed or sourced. Movable religious dates still require region-specific calendar extraction.

coverage_policy: Do not claim all global festivals are covered. Keep discovery gaps visible, and never render placeholder records as events.
important_data_rules: Festival master identities are separate from annual occurrence dates.
Do not materialize a variable date unless an authoritative or clearly identified calendar supports the year and region.
For dates beginning at sundown, retain local-calendar semantics; do not blindly shift Gregorian date by timezone.
Do not merge similar observances across traditions without evidence.
A source URL must support the specific date or stable cultural description; review source coverage before public release.
Placeholder coverage records must not render as actual events.

source_strategy.use: Documented cultural practices and community festivals; not a complete event calendar.
Generate Jewish annual and minor observances, with attribution and date semantics.
Indian Hindu/Sikh/Islamic/Christian calendar listings; verify regional setting and year.
International Vesak context; national Buddhist observances can differ.

festivals.name: Gahambar seasonal festivals
festivals.significance: Six seasonal festivals commemorating creation and community sharing; dates differ by calendar tradition.

festivals.name: Khordad Sal
festivals.significance: Commemorates the birth of Zoroaster; dates differ by calendar tradition.

festivals.name: Jamshedi / Fasli Nowruz
festivals.significance: Zoroastrian New Year under the Fasli calendar, aligned with the spring equinox.

festivals.name: Osun-Osogbo Festival
festivals.significance: Annual festival honoring Osun, with processions and rites at the sacred grove.
festivals.date_rule_or_notes: Usually August; exact schedule announced locally

festivals.name: Homowo Festival
festivals.significance: Harvest festival associated with remembrance of famine and communal renewal.
festivals.date_rule_or_notes: Local schedule varies by Ga community

festivals.name: Timkat / Ethiopian Epiphany
festivals.significance: Celebrates the baptism of Jesus with processions and water-blessing ceremonies.
festivals.date_rule_or_notes: Usually 19 January Gregorian; some leap-year calendar nuance

festivals.name: Meskel
festivals.significance: Commemorates the finding of the True Cross; associated with the Demera bonfire.
festivals.date_rule_or_notes: Usually 27 September Gregorian; 28 September in Ethiopian leap-year context

festivals.name: Ganna / Ethiopian Christmas
festivals.significance: Celebrates the Nativity of Christ in the Ethiopian Orthodox tradition.

festivals.name: Fasika / Ethiopian Easter
festivals.significance: Celebrates the resurrection of Jesus Christ in Ethiopian Orthodox tradition.

festivals.name: Hajj
festivals.regions: Muslim communities worldwide; rites in Mecca, Saudi Arabia
festivals.significance: Annual pilgrimage to Mecca, a pillar of Islam for those able to perform it.
festivals.date_rule_or_notes: 8–13 Dhu al-Hijjah; lunar calendar and official Saudi announcements

festivals.name: Islamic New Year / 1 Muharram
festivals.significance: Marks the beginning of the Hijri year.
festivals.date_rule_or_notes: 1 Muharram; local calendar authority or moon sighting

festivals.name: Laylat al-Bara'ah / Mid-Sha'ban
festivals.regions: Some Muslim communities in South Asia, Middle East and elsewhere
festivals.significance: Night of devotion and prayer observed in some Muslim traditions; status and practices vary.

festivals.name: Newroz / Kurdish New Year
festivals.regions: Kurdish communities across Turkey, Iraq, Iran, Syria and diaspora
festivals.significance: Celebrates spring and Kurdish cultural identity, often with bonfires, music and dancing.

quality_gates: Every displayed occurrence must have a source URL and a region/calendar convention.
Never use a fixed date for a movable observance unless a specific year and region support it.
Generate Jewish occurrences using Hebcal API with major, minor, modern holidays, minor fasts, Rosh Chodesh, special Shabbatot and Yom Kippur Katan options, retaining attribution.
Generate Islamic dates from a clearly named Hijri calendar (e.g. Umm al-Qura) and mark local moon-sighting-dependent observances as observation-dependent.
Generate Hindu festival occurrences separately by regional panchang (e.g. Andhra Pradesh/Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Bengal, Maharashtra, Nepal) and retain calendar authority.
Generate Christian movable feasts using explicit Western, Orthodox and Ethiopian calendar rules; never merge their dates.
Add source-reviewed annual dates for every Buddhist, Jain, Sikh, Bahá’í and Zoroastrian observance and distinguish denominations and regional conventions.
Add local/Indigenous festivals as individual named records with community/location and community-approved sources; placeholders are not events.
Check every occurrence date and multi-day range; no invented date rows.
Audit month-by-month coverage and publish a separate gap register before claiming completeness.
